name: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
request: Create a small, playable Sky Steps checkpoint parkour game for one player on desktop and touch. Build one coherent short course with three ordered checkpoints, a moving-platform crossing, a clearly marked fall hazard, and a finish. Players must physically traverse it; touching a later checkpoint early must not skip progress. Reaching a checkpoint shows visible activation animation and synchronized confirmation sound. Falling returns the player to the last valid checkpoint without losing progress. Show the current checkpoint and elapsed run time, then a completion result and deliberate replay control. Search Marketplace first for reusable checkpoint, moving-platform and course components, preserving useful existing behavior, visuals, motion and media. Inspect what is included and integrate missing rules rather than replacing working components wholesale. Use Marketplace audio and verify it actually plays. If a suitable component cannot be imported faithfully, record that capability gap. Use compact readable geometry and comfortable jumps; choose reasonable style and layout yourself. No multiplayer, saving, purchases or sprawling map. Success needs native traversal, ordered progression, moving-platform behavior, fall recovery, finish/replay and legible desktop/touch UI. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.

assetNeeds.role: Reusable checkpoint system or obby checkpoint component that may supply beacon geometry, touch behavior, activation animation, progression interfaces, and embedded confirmation media for the three ordered checkpoints.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must be inspectable and retainable inside Workspace/Forge_c405e7e9b70b. Prefer a compact component with source-visible behavior, numbered or easily distinguishable checkpoints, clear dormant and active states, and no datastore, monetization, admin, or competitive dependencies. Audit all scripts and dependencies; ordered progression, server validation, respawn integration, animation, and media claims require native verification. Unsupported serialization or hidden dependencies are capability gaps, not permission to rebuild it procedurally.

intent.interaction: The player physically touches the next valid checkpoint; the server accepts it, the beacon visibly activates, confirmation audio begins, and the new location becomes the fall-recovery destination. Early and repeated touches produce no progress reward.

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with complete reusable Model searches for checkpoint systems, moving-platform systems, and compact sky-obstacle courses, because these may include the requested geometry, scripts, motion, activation animation, reset hooks, and sound references. Inspect candidate hierarchies and source code, reject arbitrary HTTP or numeric require dependencies, identify unsupported serialization, and test existing behavior before assigning glue scripts or designing replacements. Preserve useful verified behavior and media rather than rebuilding imported components wholesale.

Audio remains a separate required asset obligation even if a checkpoint component includes it. Prefer captured audio from a retained checkpoint component, then search Marketplace separately if no suitable included cue exists. The chosen sound must retain provenance and pass loading, playback, and listening checks. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; checkpoint animation should come from an inspectable Model when available. Any necessary authored visual tween or integration may only be decided after inspection establishes that equivalent reusable behavior is absent and the asset pipeline records the sourcing result. Import failures, hidden dependencies, unsupported behavior, or failed audio verification must be reported as capability gaps rather than treated as authorization for a procedural substitute.
spec.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
spec.summary:
A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and complete obby/course components must be searched and inspected before implementation decisions. Useful verified geometry, scripts, motion, animation, and media will be retained. Unsupported scripts, missing dependencies, failed audio playback, or behavior that cannot be imported faithfully are explicit capability gaps and do not authorize an unverified procedural substitute.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a clean, optimistic high-altitude aesthetic with compact floating islands and a clearly readable forward route. Main traversable surfaces use pale cloud-white and cool cyan materials; structural undersides use deeper blue-violet tones to give each island a designed silhouette. Checkpoints are tall numbered beacon assemblies with dormant cyan rings and a vivid green-white activated state. The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

The HUD is compact and readable on desktop and touch: a top-center checkpoint label such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3,” a large tabular elapsed time beneath it, and restrained status messaging. On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens. Do not cover the central jump view during active play.

tasks.title: Search Marketplace for complete obby/checkpoint systems, moving-platform components, and compact sky-course kits before designing replacement implementation. Inspect promising candidates for geometry, scripts, interfaces, animations, media, dependencies, and import fidelity; record explicit capability gaps.

Audit imported candidates inside the namespace, test their existing checkpoint behavior, platform motion and carry behavior, animations, and embedded sound references, then decide exactly which verified features are retained and which requested integration rules remain missing.

Assemble the compact floating route under Workspace/Forge_c405e7e9b70b using retained verified components: safe Start island, introductory steps, Checkpoint 1, moving crossing to Checkpoint 2, ascending steps to Checkpoint 3, finish arch, and marked hazard and recovery volume. Preserve imported component hierarchy and avoid unrelated place objects.

After component inspection, implement only the missing authoritative integration for Start, ordered checkpoint acceptance, anti-skip validation, fall recovery, finish validation, authoritative timing, replay, respawn, rate limits, and per-player cleanup. Register necessary glue paths only after retained interfaces are known.

Integrate and tune the retained moving-platform component as a mandatory crossing, preserving verified motion and character-carry behavior. Validate route endpoints, cycle readability, safe boarding and dismount, reset behavior, and server ownership; report a capability gap instead of silently replacing behavior if faithful import fails.

Connect accepted server progression to each retained checkpoint's visible activation behavior and the verified Marketplace confirmation sound. Ensure animation and audible playback begin in the same activation phase and do not trigger on invalid or repeated touches.

Create the persistent responsive HUD for checkpoint progress, elapsed time, status feedback, completion result, and deliberate mouse or touch Replay input. Bind to authoritative replicated state, initialize from current state, and rebind character-dependent presentation without duplicate interfaces.

Apply the coordinated sky-step palette, silhouettes, route landmarks, hazard warnings, checkpoint numbering, dormant and active visual hierarchy, finish focal treatment, lighting, and safe-area-aware HUD styling without obstructing traversal.

Run protected native gameplay verification for the complete loop on desktop and touch: physical traversal, early-checkpoint rejection, all activation feedback, audible Marketplace sound, moving-platform carry, fall recovery at every stage, premature finish rejection, completion timing, replay, reset, respawn, cleanup, and required-instance presence. Report all untestable or failed asset capabilities honestly.
